documents.title: Office Visit: Knee pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Right knee has been getting steadily worse for about six months. Hurts with walking and stairs, eases when she sits. Getting out of a chair after a long sit is the hard part. Both knees stiff in the morning but loosen within 20 minutes. No swelling, no locking, no injury.
Hands about the same on acetaminophen.
Smoking 1 ppd. Weight unchanged, BMI 33.
O: BP/HR as charted. Knees: mild crepitus and tenderness over the medial joint line on both sides, no warmth, no effusion, full extension, flexion to ~115. Gait normal. Strength, reflexes and sensation in the legs normal.
X-rays both knees today (in-office): joint space narrowing and osteophytes bilaterally.
A/P:
1. Osteoarthritis, both knees (R symptomatic). She asked what she can do to cut the long-term toll rather than just patching pain. Discussed: weight loss is the biggest lever (each pound off is several off the knee), quadriceps strengthening, low-impact activity. PT referral placed for a home program. Continue acetaminophen as needed; topical options if needed later.
2. T2DM -- A1c today (due).
3. Tobacco -- also slows healing of everything; counseled.
F/u 3 mo.

PHYSICAL THERAPY INITIAL EVALUATION -- 06/20/2022
Dx: bilateral knee osteoarthritis, R>L.
Subjective: pain with stairs and rising from low chairs; morning stiffness under half an hour. Goal: walk a mile without stopping.
Objective: quad strength 4/5 R, 4+/5 L. Knee flexion R 112, L 118 degrees. Sit-to-stand x5 in 16 seconds with arm use.
Plan: 6-8 visits over 6 weeks. Quad sets, straight leg raises, mini-squats, stationary bike; home exercise program issued.

documents.title: Orthopedic Consultation
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
ORTHOPEDICS & SPORTS MEDICINE -- new visit 12/06/2022
Referred by PCP for right knee.

HPI: Chronic right knee osteoarthritis, first worked up by her internist six months ago, now acutely worse with more stiffness. Pain for roughly six months that worsens with activity and settles with rest; morning stiffness about 20 minutes.
PMH: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, glaucoma, hand osteoarthritis. Meds: HCTZ, metformin, atorvastatin, latanoprost, acetaminophen. NKDA.
Social: smoker, 35 pack-years.
BMI 32.

Exam (right knee): bony enlargement; tender at the medial joint line; crepitus through flexion and extension; passive and active motion limited by pain. No warmth, no erythema. Ligaments stable.
Imaging: right knee films today show joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes.

Assessment: Flare of right knee osteoarthritis.
Plan: Relative rest from long periods of standing; restart the home strengthening program; acetaminophen; ice after activity. Follow up as needed.

documents.title: Sick Visit: Rash
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Two days of burning on the right side of her chest wrapping toward the back, then blisters came up this morning. No fever. No eye symptoms. Never had the shingles shot.
O: Afebrile. Grouped vesicles on an erythematous base in a band along the right T5 dermatome, front to back, not crossing midline. No lesions on face/nose. Rest of skin clear.
A/P: Herpes zoster, right T5, within 72 h. Valacyclovir 1 g TID x 7 days. Acetaminophen for pain; cool compresses. Keep lesions covered around anyone pregnant or immunocompromised. Call if spreading, eye involvement, or pain uncontrolled. Shingrix after this settles -- she says now she'll take it.

documents.title: Shingles
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Blisters are crusting over. Still burns. Finished 5 days of the pills, 2 to go. Is it okay to go to my sister's cookout?

documents.title: RE: Shingles
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Once every blister has crusted over you're no longer contagious, so yes if they're all crusted. Finish the full 7 days. Let us know if the pain isn't easing.

documents.body: The shingles blisters are gone but the burning on my right side is still there, worse when my shirt rubs it. Tylenol and Advil don't touch it. Is this normal?

documents.title: RE: Still burning
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Dorothy, nerve pain after shingles can linger. The doctor would like to see you -- we have 9/12 at 2:00. Loose cotton layers over the area can help in the meantime.

documents.title: Office Visit: Post-zoster pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Rash from July healed, but burning and jabbing pain persist in the same band on her right chest. Clothing touching it is the worst. OTC acetaminophen and ibuprofen tried -- no help. Sleeping poorly.
O: Healed hyperpigmented marks along right T5. Exquisitely sensitive to light touch in that band. Lungs clear.
A/P:
1. Persistent pain after zoster, 2+ months. Options discussed; she'd rather see neurology before starting a nerve medication, given her worries about feeling foggy. Referral placed. Stop the ibuprofen.
2. T2DM -- A1c, BMP today.

documents.title: Neurology Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROLOGY CONSULTATION -- 12/05/2023
Referral: persistent pain after shingles.

67-year-old woman with glaucoma and osteoarthritis. About five months ago she had shingles on the right chest, treated with valacyclovir; the pain never went away. It is sharp and shooting, and even light touch sets it off. Over-the-counter acetaminophen and ibuprofen have not helped.
Other history: hypertension (HCTZ), type 2 diabetes (metformin), hyperlipidemia. Smoker, 35 pack-years. NKDA.

Exam: hyperpigmentation and scarring in the right T5 dermatome. A cotton swab drawn lightly across the area produces severe pain (allodynia). Strength, reflexes and sensation otherwise normal. No active lesions.

Assessment: Postherpetic neuralgia, right T5. Acute zoster resolved.
Plan: Gabapentin 300 mg at bedtime, increasing every 5 days to 300 mg three times daily. Counseled on dizziness and sleepiness; take care on stairs, no driving if drowsy. Follow up in 3 months, or PCP can continue if stable.
